species.name: Green Sea Turtle
species.intro: Nests on Malaysian beaches. Adults graze on seagrass.

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Green turtles forage in shallow coastal waters and seagrass meadows; females nest on sandy beaches.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: They can swallow plastic or become tangled in discarded gear, but this page does not document an injured turtle here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic off the beach, report lost gear, and watch turtles from a distance.

species.conservationMessage: Reducing discarded litter may reduce general wildlife risks. This card does not record local harm or ecological recovery.
species.habitat: Green turtles forage in shallow coastal waters and seagrass meadows; females nest on sandy beaches.
species.threatStatus: See approved sources; no local threat assessment is made.

species.name: Irrawaddy Dolphin
species.intro: A round head and no beak. Lives close to shore.

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Irrawaddy dolphins use shallow coastal waters and river mouths.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Entanglement in fishing nets is documented; no local injured dolphin is shown, and active nets are not necessarily litter.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Report lost nets and watch dolphins from a distance.

species.habitat: Irrawaddy dolphins use shallow coastal waters and river mouths.
species.threatStatus: See approved sources; no local threat assessment is made.

species.name: Moorish Idol
species.intro: Long white fin and bold black bands. Grazes on reef sponges.

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Moorish idols inhabit lagoons, reef flats, and rocky or coral reefs.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Marine litter can harm reef habitats, but no species-specific or local injury record is shown here.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Take your litter away and do not step on coral.

species.threatStatus: See approved sources; no local threat assessment is made.

species.name: Ocellaris Clownfish
species.intro: Shelters in sea anemones and rarely strays far from them.

answers.title: Where It Lives
answers.text: Ocellaris clownfish live among sea anemones on shallow coral reefs.

answers.title: Litter Impact
answers.text: Lab-reared juveniles ingested microplastics, but this does not show harm at this reef.

answers.title: What You Can Do
answers.text: Keep plastic out of the sea and avoid touching anemones or corals.

risks.explanation: Reported plastic may create an ingestion risk for sea turtles, marine birds and fish. General literature does not establish harm at this beach.
risks.practicalTip: Collect discarded plastic where safe, and keep away from wildlife.

risks.explanation: Discarded fishing gear may entangle sea turtles, marine mammals, marine birds and fish. This is general risk context, not evidence of local injury.
risks.practicalTip: Report lost fishing gear; do not handle an entangled animal and contact the relevant authority.
